candidates: Avoid magic numeric literals for config-derived values in diagram code (e.g., a bare `2` multiplying a padding value). Instead, expose such values as named properties in the diagram's default config object, following the same pattern used by other diagrams in the project (e.g., `pieDb.ts` and its corresponding defaults).
Throw errors directly with `throw new Error(...)` rather than first assigning the error to a local variable when that variable serves no purpose other than to be thrown on the very next line.

Access diagram config default values consistently across the codebase. Some diagrams (e.g., `pieDb.ts`) import `defaultConfig` from `defaultConfig.ts` as an explicit fallback; prefer that established pattern over ad-hoc optional-chaining + nullish-coalescing scattered throughout rendering and DB modules. Avoid introducing helper types that claim to represent 'defaults' but actually return the current (possibly user-overridden) configuration, as these names are misleading.

Avoid patching third-party dependencies directly in the repository (e.g., via `pnpm patchedDependencies`). When a dependency lacks a necessary feature (such as a missing ESM `exports` field), raise an upstream PR first. If a temporary in-repo patch is unavoidable, document clearly why native support is absent and link to the open upstream issue or PR.

In diagram renderers, use the existing `selectSvgElement` utility from `rendering-util/selectSvgElement.ts` to obtain the SVG element for a diagram ID. Do not reimplement the sandbox/`securityLevel` SVG-selection logic inline in individual renderer files.

When a diagram renderer appends a `<g>` element to an SVG, type the result as `Group` (imported from `diagram-api/types.ts`) rather than as `SVG` or a generic `D3Element`, to accurately reflect the DOM structure.

Annotate diagram `draw` functions with the `DrawDefinition` (or `DiagramRenderer`) type and diagram styles functions with `DiagramStylesProvider`, both from `diagram-api/types.ts`, rather than writing ad-hoc or implicit function signatures.

SVG/D3 attribute values can legally be either strings or numbers. Ensure that diagram node and shape property type definitions use an appropriate `string | number` union rather than narrowing to only `number` when string values are also valid, to avoid incorrect type errors at call sites.
